title: Fix CowData reader thread-safety / crash — assignment now "observably atomic"

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body: `CowData` is intended to be thread safe, but currently that is not the case. This PR fixes a thread-safety issue for reading whilst a write takes place and prevents real-world (sporadic) engine crashes. **Note:** This PR only addresses thread-safety of readers (whilst one other thread writes). `CowData` is still _not thread-safe for multiple writers_ i.e. multiple concurrent assignments can still lead to a double free / crash. # The problem When assigning to `CowData` previously it would first `_unref` before taking on the new reference. `_unref` would leave the `CowData` ptr as `nullptr`. If another thread attempted to obtain their own reference to this `CowData`, they'd unexpectedly end up with a `nullptr`. # Specific example: Android camera feed Crash, accessing a `Vector`. _Sorry, the screenshot shows the stacktrace and a `SIGTRAP` but we're not we're not observing the top frame in the screenshot. Still, we can see a crash occurred accessing a (nullptr) vector._ Let's see what's going on... ## GLThread We're attempting to update an OpenGL texture, this update was stored in the command queue (inserted by the ImageReader thread). It's being processed on the GLThread. Annotation (1) in the image we can see the assignment. Annotation (2) shows the value read. It was a `nullptr`. This should _never_ be the case. The image should always have a valid value. If we look at Annotation (3), we can see the image _does_ actually have a valid value when we crash. Thus it must have previously been a `nullptr` but has changed since. Why...? ## ImageReader This thread has just updated our image and is currently waiting for the command queue lock to push the new texture data. That means it has just recently called `initialize_data` on our `Image`. An operation that _should_ essentially be observed to outsiders like an atomic swap of the underlying image data. In practice, its implementation assigns the `p_data` (a `Vector`) to its own `data`. `Vector`'s assignment operator then assigns its underlying `_cowdata` and we end up in the troublesome `_ref` implementation that briefly points our `CowData` at a `nullptr` unnecessarily i.e. not an "atomic" swap. # The Fix We no longer call `_unref` on the `CowData` instance during assignment. We of course do still need to free our previously pointed to data, but this logic has been extracted out into a static `_unref`. We call this last though _after_ we've assigned the new pointer to the `CowData`. We no longer have an intermediary `nullptr` state. **_Now_ there's actually a second related bug.** What happens if another thread grabs our `_ptr` and is in the process of incrementing the reference count but our thread doing the assignment wins the race i.e. obtains a new value AND decrements the reference count before the other thread increments? This was _partially_ handled before. The new assignment would have just silently never gone through, since we previously ran `_unref` though, you'd unexpectedly end up with `nullptr`. That's fine if the source `CowData` had actually been cleared (rather than reassigned), but we should NOT end up with a `nullptr` just because another thread happened to assign just as we read. Fortunately, we can detect this situation. ~This PR introduces a loop in `_ref`. >99.99% of the time we won't ever loop. _But_ what the loop does is requery from the source `CowData` if a buffer is unexpectedly freed before we can obtain a reference to it. Now, that may genuinely happen if the source `CowData` is `clear()`d, and this is correctly handled by checking if the new value is a `nullptr` and bailing out. But otherwise, we try claim the latest value again.~ **EDIT:** Implementation has been updated to instead use a lock-free (for readers) cross-thread signaling implementation, paired with a memory barrier that guarantees the `_ref` we're trying to claim is valid (assuming no unsupported parallel writes took place). Collectively this PR basically fixes swapping / double buffering in many places through-out the engine. ## Fix observed in practice The Android camera crash is actually a bit easier to reproduce than I would have thought. So I was fortunately able to place a break point that shows where a crash would have _previously_ occurred, but is now being handled correctly. Here we can see we failed to increment the reference count of the buffer we're attempting to claim. We can see the cause of this, the `p_from._ptr` has changed out from under us. That's fine. We're stopped on a line of code that'll grab the new value and try again. The above shows the loop passing back through and claiming the newly updated buffer i.e. no unexpected `nullptr`s for us anymore. Yay! This probably fixes quite a few sporadic crashes people have run into for otherwise unexplained reasons. One issue closely related and presumably fixed: Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/93125
